one_liner: Crystalline sweetener from sugarcane or sugar beets.
why_used: Adds sweetness, aids browning, acts as a preservative in high concentrations, and provides bulk and texture.
origin_note: Extracted from sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum) or sugar beet (Beta vulgaris).

one_liner: Liquid sweetener made from corn starch with boosted fructose.
why_used: Provides sweetness, improves moisture retention, extends shelf life, and is cheaper than sugar in many regions.
origin_note: Derived from corn (maize) starch through enzymatic processing.
region_notes: Banned or restricted in some EU countries; widely used in the United States.

one_liner: Ground wheat kernels used as a staple baking ingredient.
why_used: Provides structure via gluten, absorbs liquid, and forms the base of breads, cakes, and pastries.
origin_note: Milled from common wheat (Triticum aestivum) grains.

one_liner: Finely milled rice used as a gluten-free flour alternative.
why_used: Acts as a gluten-free base for baking, thickens sauces, and provides a light crispy coating.
origin_note: Milled from raw rice grains (Oryza sativa).

one_liner: White powdery starch extracted from corn kernels.
why_used: Thickens sauces and gravies, provides a crisp coating, and stabilises fillings in baked goods.
origin_note: Extracted from the endosperm of corn (Zea mays) kernels.

one_liner: Semi-solid tropical oil from oil palm fruit.
why_used: Provides texture and mouthfeel, extends shelf life, is heat-stable for frying, and is cost-effective.
origin_note: Pressed from the mesocarp of oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) fruit.
region_notes: Subject to sustainability concerns; RSPO certification exists for responsibly sourced palm oil.

one_liner: Light cooking oil pressed from sunflower seeds.
why_used: Provides a neutral flavour, withstands high heat, and is used in frying, baking, and dressings.
origin_note: Pressed from the seeds of the sunflower (Helianthus annuus).

one_liner: Neutral-flavoured oil from rapeseed cultivars low in erucic acid.
why_used: Provides a mild flavour, high smoke point, and a favourable omega-3 to omega-6 ratio for cooking and baking.
origin_note: Extracted from seeds of canola (Brassica napus) cultivars.

one_liner: Flavourful oil pressed from ripe olives.
why_used: Adds rich flavour to dishes, used in dressings and sautéing, and valued for its monounsaturated fat content.
origin_note: Cold-pressed from the fruit of the olive tree (Olea europaea).

one_liner: Tropical oil extracted from coconut meat, solid at room temperature.
why_used: Provides a rich texture, is heat-stable for frying, and adds a subtle coconut flavour to foods.
origin_note: Extracted from the dried meat (copra) or fresh flesh of the coconut (Cocos nucifera).
region_notes: The FDA classifies coconut as a tree nut for allergen labelling purposes.

one_liner: Essential mineral seasoning used in virtually all foods.
why_used: Enhances flavour, acts as a preservative, controls yeast fermentation, and strengthens gluten in dough.
origin_note: Mined from underground salt deposits or evaporated from seawater.

one_liner: The most fundamental ingredient in food preparation.
why_used: Acts as a solvent, hydrates dry ingredients, enables chemical reactions, and controls texture and consistency.
origin_note: Sourced from municipal water supplies, springs, or wells and purified.

one_liner: Unprocessed cow's milk containing its natural fat content.
why_used: Adds richness, moisture, and tenderness to baked goods, and provides protein and calcium in beverages and sauces.
origin_note: Obtained from dairy cows (Bos taurus) by milking.

one_liner: Dehydrated milk with fat removed, used as a shelf-stable dairy ingredient.
why_used: Adds milk solids and protein without extra moisture, improves texture in baked goods, and extends shelf life.
origin_note: Produced by removing water and fat from pasteurised cow's milk.

one_liner: Dried by-product of cheese-making, rich in milk proteins.
why_used: Adds protein, improves browning, enhances flavour, and improves texture in baked goods and processed foods.
origin_note: By-product of cheese or casein production from cow's milk.

one_liner: Solid dairy fat made by churning cream.
why_used: Provides rich flavour, flaky texture in pastries, aids browning, and acts as a tenderiser in baked goods.
origin_note: Churned from cream separated from cow's milk.

one_liner: High-fat layer skimmed from whole milk.
why_used: Adds richness and smoothness to sauces, soups, desserts, and beverages.
origin_note: Separated from the fat-rich layer of whole cow's milk.

one_liner: Versatile ingredient providing structure, leavening, and emulsification.
why_used: Binds ingredients, provides leavening through trapped air, emulsifies fats and liquids, and adds colour and richness.
origin_note: Laid by domestic chickens (Gallus gallus domesticus).

one_liner: Fatty emulsifier extracted from soybean oil.
why_used: Prevents separation of oil and water, improves texture, reduces stickiness, and extends shelf life in chocolate and baked goods.
origin_note: Extracted as a by-product of soybean (Glycine max) oil refining.

one_liner: Highly refined soy protein used to boost protein content.
why_used: Increases protein content, improves texture and moisture retention, and acts as a meat extender in processed foods.
origin_note: Extracted and purified from defatted soybean (Glycine max) meal.

one_liner: Mildly sweet starch derivative used as a filler and thickener.
why_used: Adds bulk, improves mouthfeel, aids in encapsulating flavours, and serves as a quick-dissolving carrier.
origin_note: Produced by partial hydrolysis of starch, typically from corn, rice, or wheat.
ambiguity_note: May be derived from wheat starch in some regions, which could introduce gluten traces.
region_notes: In the EU, wheat-derived maltodextrin is common. In the US, corn-derived is standard.

one_liner: Simple sugar identical to glucose, derived from corn starch.
why_used: Provides quick sweetness, aids browning, feeds yeast in fermentation, and serves as a carrier for seasonings.
origin_note: Produced by complete hydrolysis of corn (maize) starch.

one_liner: Thick, sweet syrup made by breaking down starch.
why_used: Prevents crystallisation in confectionery, adds sweetness and body, and improves moisture retention.
origin_note: Produced by hydrolysis of starch, typically from corn or wheat.
ambiguity_note: May be derived from wheat in some regions, potentially containing trace gluten.
region_notes: Wheat-derived glucose syrup is more common in Europe; corn-derived in the US.

one_liner: Tart acid naturally found in citrus fruits, produced by fermentation.
why_used: Adds sour flavour, regulates pH, acts as a preservative, and enhances the effectiveness of other antioxidants.
origin_note: Commercially produced by fermenting sugars using the mould Aspergillus niger.

one_liner: Vitamin C used as an antioxidant and dough improver.
why_used: Prevents oxidation and browning, strengthens gluten in bread dough, and serves as a nutritional supplement.
origin_note: Commercially synthesised from glucose via the Reichstein process or fermentation.

one_liner: Synthetic preservative effective against moulds and yeasts.
why_used: Inhibits growth of moulds, yeasts, and some bacteria in acidic foods like soft drinks, pickles, and condiments.
origin_note: Produced by neutralising benzoic acid with sodium hydroxide.

one_liner: Widely used preservative that inhibits mould and yeast growth.
why_used: Extends shelf life by preventing mould and yeast growth in dairy, baked goods, wines, and personal care products.
origin_note: Produced by neutralising sorbic acid with potassium hydroxide.

one_liner: Bread preservative that inhibits mould growth.
why_used: Prevents mould and bacterial rope formation in bread and baked goods, extending shelf life without affecting taste.
origin_note: Produced by reacting propionic acid with calcium hydroxide.

one_liner: Polysaccharide thickener produced by bacterial fermentation.
why_used: Thickens and stabilises sauces and dressings, prevents ice crystal formation, and provides a creamy mouthfeel.
origin_note: Produced by fermentation of sugars by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris.

one_liner: Plant-based thickener from guar bean seeds.
why_used: Thickens and stabilises ice cream, sauces, and gluten-free baked goods, and improves texture and shelf life.
origin_note: Extracted from the endosperm of guar beans (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba).

one_liner: Seaweed-derived gelling and thickening agent.
why_used: Gels, thickens, and stabilises dairy products, plant milks, and processed meats, providing a smooth texture.
origin_note: Extracted from red seaweed species (Chondrus crispus, Eucheuma, Kappaphycus).
region_notes: Degraded carrageenan (poligeenan) has raised health concerns; food-grade carrageenan is considered distinct.

one_liner: Natural gelling agent extracted from fruit peels.
why_used: Gels jams and jellies, stabilises acidified milk drinks, and provides a fat-like mouthfeel in low-fat products.
origin_note: Extracted from citrus peels or apple pomace.

one_liner: Animal-derived protein that gels when cooled.
why_used: Creates gels in desserts and confections, stabilises foams, binds water, and provides a smooth mouthfeel.
origin_note: Produced by hydrolysing collagen from animal skin, bones, and connective tissue (typically pork or beef, sometimes fish).
ambiguity_note: May be derived from pork, beef, or fish sources; exact source often unspecified on labels.
region_notes: Halal and kosher status depends on the animal source; pork-derived gelatin is not halal or kosher.

one_liner: Chemically or physically altered corn starch for improved performance.
why_used: Provides better stability under heat, acid, and freezing than regular starch, and improves texture in sauces and fillings.
origin_note: Corn starch treated with acids, enzymes, or cross-linking agents to alter its properties.

canonical_name: Mono- and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
names: mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
one_liner: Fat-based emulsifiers used to blend oil and water in foods.
why_used: Improves texture and consistency, prevents staling in bread, and stabilises emulsions in margarine and ice cream.
origin_note: Produced from glycerol and fatty acids, which can be from plant oils (soy, palm) or animal fats.
ambiguity_note: Can be derived from plant or animal fats; source is often unspecified on labels.
region_notes: Vegan, vegetarian, and halal status depends on the fat source, which is often unspecified.

one_liner: Chemical leavener that produces carbon dioxide when heated or acidified.
why_used: Leavens baked goods by producing CO2, neutralises acids, and tenderises by weakening gluten.
origin_note: Produced from soda ash (sodium carbonate) and carbon dioxide via the Solvay process or mined as nahcolite.

one_liner: The acid in vinegar, used as a preservative and flavouring.
why_used: Regulates acidity, acts as a preservative against bacteria, and adds a tangy flavour to condiments and pickles.
origin_note: Produced by bacterial fermentation of ethanol or synthetically from methanol.

one_liner: Acid produced by fermentation, found naturally in yoghurt and sauerkraut.
why_used: Adjusts pH, acts as a preservative, adds tartness to dairy and fermented foods, and tenderises meat.
origin_note: Commercially produced by bacterial fermentation of sugars using Lactobacillus species.
region_notes: Despite the name, commercially produced lactic acid is typically dairy-free (fermented from plant sugars).

one_liner: Naturally occurring fruit acid, commonly from grapes.
why_used: Adds tartness, stabilises colour, acts as an emulsifier in baking powder, and regulates pH in wine and candy.
origin_note: Obtained as a by-product of winemaking from grape lees and tartar deposits.

one_liner: Umami seasoning that enhances savoury flavour in foods.
why_used: Intensifies savoury (umami) taste, allows reduction of salt content, and enhances the perception of meaty flavour.
origin_note: Produced by bacterial fermentation of sugars (from molasses, starch, or sugar beets) using Corynebacterium glutamicum.
region_notes: Often stigmatised despite scientific consensus of safety at typical intake levels.

one_liner: Brown colouring made by heating sugars.
why_used: Provides brown colour to soft drinks, sauces, baked goods, and confectionery without significantly affecting flavour.
origin_note: Produced by controlled heat treatment of carbohydrates (glucose, sucrose, or corn syrup).
region_notes: E150a (plain caramel) is the simplest class. E150c and E150d use ammonia and may raise health concerns.

one_liner: Natural red-orange colouring extracted from paprika peppers.
why_used: Adds red-orange colour to sauces, snacks, and processed meats without synthetic dyes.
origin_note: Extracted from dried sweet red peppers (Capsicum annuum).

one_liner: Natural yellow-orange colour from annatto seeds.
why_used: Provides yellow-orange colour to cheese, butter, margarine, and baked goods as an alternative to synthetic dyes.
origin_note: Extracted from the seed coat of the achiote tree (Bixa orellana).

one_liner: Orange pigment and provitamin A used as a natural colouring.
why_used: Adds yellow-orange colour to margarine, beverages, and dairy products, and serves as a source of vitamin A.
origin_note: Extracted from carrots, palm oil, or algae, or produced synthetically.
ambiguity_note: Can be naturally extracted or synthetically produced; source may not always be specified.

one_liner: White pigment used to brighten and opacify foods.
why_used: Provides bright white colour and opacity to confectionery coatings, icing, and chewing gum.
origin_note: Derived from ilmenite or rutile mineral ores and purified to food-grade specifications.
region_notes: Banned as a food additive in the EU since 2022 due to safety concerns. Still permitted in the US and many other countries.

one_liner: Pale yellow fat extracted from cocoa beans.
why_used: Gives chocolate its snap and melt-in-mouth quality, and is used in confections and cosmetics.
origin_note: Pressed from roasted, fermented cocoa beans (Theobroma cacao).

one_liner: Dry powder made from pressed cocoa solids.
why_used: Provides chocolate flavour and colour to baked goods, beverages, and desserts.
origin_note: Made from cocoa solids remaining after cocoa butter is extracted from cocoa beans (Theobroma cacao).

one_liner: Aromatic extract from cured vanilla bean pods.
why_used: Adds a complex, sweet aroma and flavour to baked goods, desserts, and beverages.
origin_note: Extracted from cured seed pods of the vanilla orchid (Vanilla planifolia).
region_notes: Contains alcohol, which may be a concern for halal diets. Alcohol-free versions exist.

one_liner: Flavouring substances derived from natural plant or animal sources.
why_used: Enhances or imparts specific flavours to foods without using synthetic chemicals.
origin_note: Derived from plant or animal sources through extraction, distillation, or fermentation. Exact source varies widely.
ambiguity_note: The term 'natural flavours' is a broad category; exact sources (plant vs. animal) are rarely disclosed.
region_notes: The vague nature of this label makes it impossible to guarantee any dietary compliance without contacting the manufacturer.

one_liner: Synthetically produced flavouring compounds.
why_used: Provides consistent, cost-effective flavouring that mimics natural tastes without reliance on natural sourcing.
origin_note: Chemically synthesised in laboratories to replicate specific flavour compounds.
ambiguity_note: Specific chemicals used are rarely disclosed on labels; composition varies by manufacturer.
region_notes: Regulations for artificial flavours vary widely between the US (FDA) and EU (EFSA).

one_liner: Living fungus that leavens bread through fermentation.
why_used: Ferments sugars to produce CO2 for leavening bread, and contributes complex flavours through fermentation by-products.
origin_note: Cultivated from the single-celled fungus Saccharomyces cerevisiae on molasses or grain substrates.

one_liner: Chemical leavening mix of acid and base that produces CO2.
why_used: Leavens cakes, muffins, and quick breads without requiring yeast, providing consistent rise and texture.
origin_note: A dry mixture of sodium bicarbonate, an acid salt (such as cream of tartar or sodium aluminium sulphate), and a starch buffer.
region_notes: Some formulations contain corn starch; aluminium-free versions are available.

one_liner: Sweet, syrupy alcohol used as a humectant and sweetener.
why_used: Retains moisture, prevents drying, adds sweetness, improves texture, and acts as a solvent for flavours.
origin_note: By-product of soap making or biodiesel production from plant oils or animal fats; also produced synthetically.
ambiguity_note: Can be from plant oils (soy, palm, coconut) or animal fats; source often unspecified.
region_notes: Vegetable glycerin is explicitly plant-derived; generic glycerol may be animal-derived.

one_liner: Sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener and humectant.
why_used: Provides sweetness with fewer calories, retains moisture, acts as a sugar substitute in sugar-free products.
origin_note: Produced by catalytic hydrogenation of glucose, typically derived from corn starch.
region_notes: Excessive consumption may cause gastrointestinal discomfort due to its laxative effect.

one_liner: Artificial sweetener about 200 times sweeter than sugar.
why_used: Provides intense sweetness with virtually no calories, used in diet drinks, sugar-free gum, and low-calorie foods.
origin_note: Synthesised from two amino acids: L-aspartic acid and L-phenylalanine methyl ester.
region_notes: Must carry a warning for people with phenylketonuria (PKU) as it contains phenylalanine.

one_liner: Artificial sweetener about 600 times sweeter than sugar.
why_used: Provides intense sweetness with zero calories, is heat-stable for baking, and does not promote tooth decay.
origin_note: Produced by selective chlorination of sucrose (replacing three hydroxyl groups with chlorine atoms).

one_liner: Natural zero-calorie sweetener from the stevia plant.
why_used: Provides sweetness 200-300 times that of sugar without calories, suitable for sugar-free and low-calorie products.
origin_note: Extracted from the leaves of the stevia plant (Stevia rebaudiana).
region_notes: Whole-leaf stevia is not approved in the EU or US; only purified steviol glycosides are permitted.

one_liner: Fatty emulsifier that can come from soy, egg, or sunflower.
why_used: Blends oil and water, improves texture, reduces stickiness, and extends shelf life in chocolate and baked goods.
origin_note: Extracted from soybeans, egg yolks, sunflower seeds, or rapeseed; source varies by manufacturer.
ambiguity_note: When listed simply as 'lecithin' without a source qualifier, it could be from soy, egg, sunflower, or rapeseed.
region_notes: If sourced from sunflower, it is free of major allergens. Check label for specific source.

one_liner: Synthetic emulsifier used to blend oil and water in foods.
why_used: Stabilises emulsions in ice cream and sauces, prevents separation, and improves texture and mouthfeel.
origin_note: Produced by reacting sorbitol with ethylene oxide and oleic acid.
ambiguity_note: Oleic acid may be from plant or animal sources; source often unspecified.
region_notes: Vegan and halal status depends on the fatty acid source.

one_liner: Curing salt that preserves meat and gives it a pink colour.
why_used: Prevents growth of Clostridium botulinum, fixes the pink colour of cured meats, and adds a characteristic cured flavour.
origin_note: Produced by reacting sodium hydroxide with nitrous acid or by reduction of sodium nitrate.
region_notes: Strictly regulated due to potential formation of nitrosamines at high temperatures.

one_liner: Synthetic antioxidant that prevents fats from going rancid.
why_used: Delays oxidation and rancidity in fats and oils, extending the shelf life of snack foods, cereals, and baked goods.
origin_note: Synthesised from 4-methoxyphenol and isobutylene.
region_notes: Classified as 'reasonably anticipated to be a human carcinogen' by the US NTP; still permitted in food at low levels.

one_liner: Synthetic antioxidant used to preserve fats and oils.
why_used: Prevents oxidative rancidity in foods containing fats, extending shelf life of cereals, snacks, and packaging materials.
origin_note: Synthesised from 4-methylphenol (p-cresol) and isobutylene.
region_notes: Banned in some countries; permitted in the US and EU at restricted levels.

one_liner: Natural mineral used as a calcium supplement and white colouring.
why_used: Fortifies foods with calcium, acts as a white colourant, regulates acidity, and serves as an anti-caking agent.
origin_note: Mined from limestone deposits or precipitated from calcium chloride and sodium carbonate.

one_liner: Essential mineral added to fortify cereals, flours, and infant foods.
why_used: Fortifies foods to prevent iron-deficiency anaemia, especially in flour, cereals, and infant formula.
origin_note: Sourced from mineral iron compounds or produced by chemical synthesis.
region_notes: Iron fortification of flour is mandatory in many countries.

one_liner: B vitamin added to enriched grains and cereals.
why_used: Fortifies foods to prevent pellagra, supports energy metabolism, and is required for enrichment of refined grains.
origin_note: Commercially synthesised from 3-methylpyridine (beta-picoline) or other chemical precursors.

one_liner: B vitamin essential for energy metabolism, added to enriched flour.
why_used: Fortifies enriched flour and cereals to prevent beriberi and support carbohydrate metabolism.
origin_note: Commercially synthesised through chemical processes involving pyrimidine and thiazole precursors.

one_liner: Yellow B vitamin used for fortification and as a food colourant.
why_used: Fortifies cereals and flour, provides yellow colour, and supports energy metabolism.
origin_note: Commercially produced by microbial fermentation using Bacillus subtilis or Ashbya gossypii.

one_liner: Synthetic B vitamin critical for cell division and fetal development.
why_used: Fortifies flour and cereals to prevent neural tube defects in pregnancy and support red blood cell formation.
origin_note: Commercially synthesised from pteridine, p-aminobenzoic acid, and glutamic acid precursors.
region_notes: Mandatory fortification of flour in the US, Canada, and many other countries.

one_liner: Primary protein found in milk, used for emulsification and nutrition.
why_used: Provides structure, emulsification, and boosts protein content.
origin_note: Precipitated from skimmed bovine milk using acid or rennet enzymes.
